says: On her laptop Alice registers her private notes source, commits a revision on the head the registration made, founds a Team there and, as its issuing authority, records on the Team's head a revocation of an earlier permit — control evidence her own device holds from the issue — and then takes a backup under access generation 7. The laptop keeps running; the backup is restored onto a second runtime, a restored copy holding the same device's data and that old access generation. The restore reports authority passive. A commit on the restored copy, expecting the head the backup holds and carrying the restored generation 7, is blocked with access_locked and access_generation_moved and moves nothing: the restored copy did not unlock itself and is not a second finalizer. Reading the profile there shows it locked because restored, at generation 8, past the one it restored. On the laptop, meanwhile, a commit expecting that same head is accepted, so the laptop stays the one runtime that moves this head. Only an explicit unlock at a terminal on the restored copy, expecting generation 8, makes its access active, as a new access state the unlock wrote at that same generation; a query there then returns the restored commit's original result and receipt. Being active at that generation is not restored authority: a hypothetical Team read the admission decider previews there, naming among its proofs the revocation record the restored copy's own backup carried, is still not admitted, with credential_revoked and control_evidence_insufficient — access being unlocked at the current generation answers only C02's own question, not whether any control evidence the restored copy holds is still current. What must not happen: the restored copy reading its restored generation as active access, unlocking without a person's explicit unlock, finalizing a commit beside the laptop, or an active access generation being read as current control authority.
